rubric.criterion: Fail: the review invents problems or omits the concrete consequences and actionable fixes for important findings. Partial: the review identifies some real concerns but leaves their project impact or fix vague. Pass: each important finding explains a concrete consequence in this ledger and gives a developer-actionable fix without invented problems. (code cannot check this because it cannot judge whether the review's explanations are grounded, useful, and free of invented concerns)

findingsKey.finding: The scheduled path appends the debit and credit through separate store calls and mutates balances between them, so a process failure can leave a persisted journal with only one side of the transfer.
The client-key lookup happens after both journal lines and balance mutations, so a retried schedule posts the movement again before it is recognized as a duplicate.
Converting the configured decimal with parseFloat and floor after multiplication can truncate values such as 0.29 to 28 minor units instead of the ledger's intended 29.
Reconciliation filters out accounts whose creation date is today even though the operations contract requires every account, allowing a new account's mismatch to go unreported.
The scheduler records a failed transfer as done and returns a done result, so the platform will not retry a transient account, balance, or store failure.
Due-time matching uses the server's local hour and minute rather than the schedule's UTC contract, so the repeated local time during a daylight-saving fallback can run a daily transfer twice.
